claim: To earn the US median household income from direct Twitch revenue alone in 2021, a streamer had to rank in roughly Twitch's top 1,322 accounts, or about the top 0.015% of active streamers.
stance_target: Content creation supports a living wage for only a vanishingly small fraction of participants
scope_conditions: Twitch only; direct-platform revenue only (subs, ads, Bits); US median household income benchmark; leak window Aug 2019 - Oct 2021; denominator is Twitch Tracker's 8.8M active streamers, not the leaked account population
quoted_support: According to the US Census Bureau, the median US household income in 2020 was $67,521. To make that much per year on Twitch, assuming you aren't bringing in money from sources not included in this data, you'd have to be one of Twitch's top 1,322 streamers right now.

claim: The leaked Twitch payout data shows steep income decay by rank: annualised, the 100th-ranked account earned about $400,000, the 200th about $270,000, the 400th under $150,000, and the 1,000th about $85,000.
stance_target: Creator income follows an extreme power-law distribution in which mean vastly exceeds median
scope_conditions: Twitch direct payouts only; ranks derived from leaked internal payout records, not a survey; figures annualised by the outlet
quoted_support: A longer copy of the unverified list seen by PC Gamer shows that the 100th most successful Twitch streamer makes approximately $400,000 per year from Twitch payouts. At 200th, the yearly gross income is around $270,000.

claim: Reporting on the Twitch leak mixes cumulative and annualised units within a single article without reconciling them, so figures from the leak are not directly comparable across outlets or even within one source.
stance_target: Quantitative claims about creator income can be cited at face value
scope_conditions: Applies to secondary reporting on the October 2021 Twitch leak
quoted_support: CriticalRole $9,626,712 ... The 100th most successful Twitch streamer makes approximately $400,000 per year from Twitch payouts.

claim: The Twitch payout leak measures only subscriptions, in-stream ads, Bits and possibly Twitch Bounty sponsorships, and excludes exclusivity contracts, self-negotiated sponsorships, merchandise, affiliate links, off-platform donations, Patreon, and all other-platform income.
stance_target: The Twitch leak represents total creator income
scope_conditions: Bounds every interpretation of the leak as an income distribution
quoted_support: the unconfirmed figures represent each streamer's cut of revenue earned from channel subscriptions, in-stream ads, Bits ... and possibly Twitch's built-in 'Bounty' system ... They can also negotiate their own sponsorships, sell merch, use affiliate links, and so on.

claim: A single professional Twitch Partner reported that direct Twitch revenue accounted for only 40% of his total streaming income, indicating the leak systematically understates total creator earnings by a large but unquantified factor.
stance_target: Platform payout records alone can measure creator income
scope_conditions: Single self-reported case, one Twitch Partner of nine years, US; not generalisable
quoted_support: Twitch is only 40% of my actual revenue.

claim: The eighth-highest earning account in the Twitch leak was not a streamer but an extension developer collecting a 20% cut of Bits spent through his product, showing the leaked ranking is of accounts rather than of individual human creators.
stance_target: Every entry in the leaked top-earner list is a content creator
scope_conditions: Twitch leak top 10; single documented case plus other corporate accounts in the top 100
quoted_support: Number eight on the list, Altoar, makes Twitch extensions. Whenever someone spends Bits through Altoar's Sound Alerts extension on a streamer's channel, for example, he gets a 20% cut.

claim: The Twitch payout leak discloses no country composition of the creator base, so it cannot be used to infer anything about creator earnings outside the US and Western Europe.
stance_target: Findings from the Twitch leak generalise to Southeast Asia
scope_conditions: Audited absence: reviewed the full PC Gamer analysis and no nationality, currency or regional breakdown appears anywhere
quoted_support: According to the US Census Bureau, the median US household income in 2020 was $67,521. To make that much per year on Twitch ... you'd have to be one of Twitch's top 1,322 streamers right now.

claim: The top 10 Twitch accounts by payout grossed between roughly $3.0 million and $9.6 million each over the roughly 26-month leak window, with the leader earning about 3.2 times the tenth-placed account.
stance_target: Creator income is extremely concentrated even within the top tail
scope_conditions: Cumulative Aug 2019 - Sept/Oct 2021; direct Twitch payouts only; unverified by Twitch
